Olga / Kim / Ben — I reviewed Catalyst's comments and drafted markups. Notes below and attached: OrderForm_Redline_v3_markups.pdf.

1) Payment terms: I prefer to avoid a blanket Net60 amendment. Proposed language for the order form: "Payment Terms: Standard Net45. For customers requesting Net60, Redwood may agree in writing provided the customer either (i) provides a 10% non-refundable deposit applied to the first invoice, or (ii) agrees to a 1% early-payment discount (incentivized by payment within 15 days). Redwood reserves the right to require additional assurances for credit exposures above $250k."

2) Invoice entity & taxes: Insert a short clause in the order form appendix: "Invoices will be issued by the Redwood entity identified on the order form. The billing entity will be Redwood Inference, Inc. (US) unless otherwise agreed in writing. Customers are responsible for any withholding taxes unless Redwood furnishes a valid tax residency certificate. For EU VAT treatment, Redwood will provide VAT invoices where applicable; the customer must notify Redwood of any VAT registration that affects invoicing."

3) Tranche/invoice acceptance: Add milestone acceptance criteria and a 10-business-day sign-off window after delivery against which invoices will be issued. If sign-off is delayed beyond 30 days, Redwood may charge an administrative hold fee of $500 per delayed invoice. (Reasonable but protects ops.)

4) Redline cleanups: I removed consumer-facing language that could be interpreted as unlimited liability and kept a short, objective acceptance definition. See attached PDF for line-by-line comments.

If you want, I can prepare two order-form PDFs: (A) standard Net45 and (B) Net60 variant with deposit/discount. I can also prepare an amendment for their legal team to sign to keep the MSA untouched.

Let me know which path you want to present and I'll generate DocuSign envelope.
